record.name: Iraq
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The Communications and Media Commission opened a draft regulation on licensing and risk-classifying AI services for consultation in September 2026, and the national AI strategy is still being revised.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.
Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. No new search or full recheck.
Checked source quotations against retained source material and documented extraction limitations; this was a partial excerpt-evidence audit, not a new search or a full recheck of the jurisdiction.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. The English search identified no qualifying institute or commitment. The CMC draft regulatory text is the selected governance evidence; the existing assessment distinguishes provider testing, classification and regulatory oversight from a national institute to evaluate advanced models. Live PDF extraction was poor; no new institutional designation was established. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Visually rechecked the three quoted headings on PDF page 2 and documented the fragmented Arabic text layer. The quotations were not changed. This was a partial evidence check, not a full record re-check.

Read all 19 articles of the CMC consultation draft from the page images during the blind sample for release 1.1.0. The draft creates no testing body. Corrected the Art. 13 note to providers or operators of general-purpose models. This was a partial evidence check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded ar query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The CMC consultation draft sets risk classification and provider testing duties. The reviewed provisions do not create an institute for evaluation of advanced models; all 19 articles were read from the page images on 19 November 2026.

related_bodies.name: Communications and Media Commission
related_bodies.role: The CMC consultation draft's contents list licensing requirements and risk classification; Iraq Business News dates the consultation to 23 September 2026. The draft is not evidence of enacted rules or an institute to evaluate advanced models.

related_bodies.name: National Centre for Artificial Intelligence
related_bodies.role: It is attached to the Prime Minister's Office; no evaluation or testing role was described in the sources read.

record.notes: The CMC draft regulation (Art. 12) sets a CMC risk-classification methodology, and Art. 13 requires providers or operators of general-purpose models to run periodic safety, security and bias tests before public release and after major changes. These are duties on providers and operators plus CMC classification; the draft creates no CMC testing body or institute for evaluating advanced models. The national AI strategy was discussed at a planning ministry meeting in April 2026, attended by the Prime Minister's adviser on AI, and was reported as under revision.
